commands.title: Open file
commands.description: Open a file in the workspace's VS Code, starting the VS Code server if needed, optionally at a line and column; this reloads the workbench. An absolute path inside another git worktree of a workspace folder switches that folder to the worktree first and opens the file there.

path.description: File to open; absolute, or relative to the current root (the selected worktree of the first workspace folder that exists, else home).

line.description: 1-based line to put the cursor on; 0 or absent keeps the default position.

col.description: 1-based column on that line; 0 or absent puts the cursor at the line start. Ignored without line.

focus.description: Also show the VS Code section and focus VS Code.

commands.title: Folder Code shows
commands.description: The workspace folder Code shows, and with folder moves Code to it, keeping that folder's selected worktree. Returns {folder, root}; folder is empty when the root is no folder's.

folder.description: A folder of the workspace, as its path. Empty reads without moving.

commands.title: Open terminal here
commands.description: Open a new terminal in the current root: the selected worktree of the first workspace folder that exists, else home.

commands.title: Restart VS Code
commands.description: Restart the VS Code server and show it again in every workspace, clearing a shown failure; VS Code's hot exit keeps unsaved edits.

commands.title: VS Code settings
commands.description: Whether the user accepted the VS Code Server License Terms: {accepted}. Read-only; consent comes only from the user's Accept & Download in the VS Code section.

accepted.description: The user accepted the VS Code Server License Terms.

commands.title: Import extensions from VS Code
commands.description: Install every extension of the desktop VS Code (code --list-extensions) that the VS Code in Clubmate doesn't have yet, from the Marketplace, one by one; returns {installed, skipped, failed: [{id, error}]} once done and reloads the VS Code section if anything was installed. Fails when the VS Code server isn't downloaded yet or an import is already running. Settings → VS Code shows the progress and the result.

failed.description: {id, error} for each extension that failed to install.
